planting.note: Plant container-grown plants or rooted cuttings in spring in well-drained, consistently moist, acidic, humus-rich soil in partial shade; Asatsuyu is a registered Japanese cultivar suited to USDA zones 7-9.

directions: Asatsuyu is a long-established Japanese green tea cultivar prized above almost all others for shaded-culture production, especially gyokuro and tencha (the base leaf for matcha), where its naturally sweet, low-astringency character and rich umami come from an unusually high theanine content that builds up when the bushes are shaded before harvest. It grows as a dense, small-leaved China-type shrub typical of fine Japanese sencha cultivars, and is processed the same way, steamed shortly after picking to halt oxidation and preserve its vivid green color. Asatsuyu has also served as a parent in later breeding programs, including the cross with Yabukita that produced the gyokuro-favored cultivar Saemidori. Give it the same acidic, humus-rich, evenly moist soil and partial shade other tea camellias prefer, with shade cloth or overhead shading applied in the weeks before harvest to maximize the sweet, low-astringency character the cultivar is prized for.
sources: Japan Tea Central Public Interest Incorporated Association
